what: A not-lose SCREEN of HYPNO v1 (the population best response, abra/regmc 1.71.0) against the same agent at equilibrium. X = gen5 at the 2 s adaptive clock with spec `hypno` (GARY v1, band 1200, the shipped gates); Y = the same spec without it. Written BEFORE the first screen game and NOT RUN by the agent that wrote it (game runs are queued: a ladder batch and an SPRT own the machine). Read ONCE, at 200 games, by read.js. No SPRT. Nothing goes on a ladder arm whatever it reads.
question: The PLAN's N2 offline sanity asks for 'its loss against an equilibrium opponent'. The arena opponent is gen5's own search, an equilibrium-seeking player that is NOT the human population GARY models, so this screen measures what HYPNO's deviations cost when the population model is wrong about the opponent. It cannot show a gain; the gain is a ladder question (PLAN N2: the per-series A/B).
why_this_release: The newest gate-passing release (OPEN 10/10, abra/regmc 1.57.0), the one the 1.67.0-1.69.0 screens and their 2 s quiet reference played.
x: solver/results/2026-10-01-gary-hypno/screen-2s-hypno.json (gen5-adaptive-2s-hypno: gen5 MAG/DODUO/PORYGON2, k 4x4, depth 0, 1 reserved switch row, budgetMs 5000 cap, adaptive { targetMs 2000, credit0Ms 667 }, hypno { model gary-v1, band 1200 })
what_differs: Only the row mix at a root: after the solve, X replaces sigma* by the best response to GARY's mass on the table's columns where GARY's (bucket, band 1200) cell passed its held-out gate, GARY covers >= 0.25 of its mass on the columns and the predicted gain beats one standard error; else X plays sigma*. Same table, same coin. The arena has no rating and no series memory, so X plays the game-1 policy at band 1200 in every game: medicham32's last recorded ladder series (solver/out/rotom/chomptopfix-2026-10-01T07-18-26-877Z, series 19-20) sat at 1269-1292, and a rated bo3 is matched near the player's own rating. At band 1200 the cells that pass are even, even_sc, behind and behind_sc; lead, single, ahead and ahead_sc play sigma*.

rule: gate.js notlose, read ONCE at 200 games: PASS iff the Wilson 95% UPPER bound of X's score is >= 0.5 (X is not shown to lose); FAIL otherwise. VOID, whatever the score, if ANY capability bar fails. A PASS is a not-lose screen, not a strength claim.

bars.text: Per arm (solver/mew/play.js ARMS, summed by gate.js `arms`): (1) prior-fallback share <= 0.05; (2) playouts per searched decision >= 161; (3) clock ratio decision_ms.x.mean / decision_ms.y.mean <= 1.10; (4) >= 190 of 200 games scored. Capability, summed over the last line of every shard (ctr.hypno, solver/mew/agent.js): (5) X's HYPNO ran: decisions > 0; (6) X's HYPNO played a best response: played > 0; (7) Y never ran it: decisions = 0. Reported, not bars: the share of X's decisions that played, were untrusted, below SE or short of coverage, the worst-case cost and the cells used.

floor_source: solver/results/2026-10-01-screens/ref-2s.result.json: the quiet 2 s reference on this release (gen5 against itself, 20 games): 364.2 and 323.2 playouts per searched decision; floor 0.5 x 323.2 = 161, as the 1.67.0 and 1.69.0 screens.
expected_direction: Slightly BELOW 0.5. Offline, on 579 held-out human positions, HYPNO deviated on 131 and cost -0.0032 win probability per decision against the table's own equilibrium column mix (solver/gary/model/gary-v1.hypno-offline.json, vs_equilibrium_opponent). If that carried to the arena at ~8 searched decisions a game the score would sit near 0.47-0.48, inside a 200-game not-lose screen's reach. A FAIL says the deviations cost real games against a non-population opponent and HYPNO stays off every arm.
on_pass: Nothing further on its own: a PASS licenses the ladder A/B that PLAN N2 names (per-series seeded, BR vs equilibrium, residual S - E), which needs Will's OK and its own pre-registration. On FAIL: report it plainly; HYPNO stays off by default.
